planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in deep, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Petruk is a government-recognized national cultivar from Jepara, Central Java, prized for small, slender seeds that leave more edible flesh per fruit.

directions: Petruk is a long-established Indonesian durian variety from Jepara, Central Java, officially recognized as a national superior cultivar for its thin, greenish-yellow husk and soft, fine-fibered yellow flesh. The flavor is intensely sweet with only mild aroma compared to many other durian, and each fruit typically holds a modest handful of small, oblong seeds, leaving proportionally more flesh to eat. Plant grafted trees in deep, well-drained, humid tropical soil in full sun, keeping moisture consistent through flowering and fruit development since erratic watering can cause fruit drop. Harvest only windfall fruit that has dropped naturally, as with other durian, rather than cutting it green from the tree.
sources: TFNet (International Tropical Fruits Network) -- Durian Varieties
Trubus Horticulture Magazine (Indonesia)
University of Hawaii CTAHR -- Durian for Hawaii

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in deep, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Sitokong originates from the Pasar Minggu/Ragunan area of Jakarta and is a recognized national superior cultivar valued for unusually thick flesh.

directions: Sitokong is a national superior durian cultivar that originated around Ragunan in the Pasar Minggu district of Jakarta, known for widely spaced spines on a moderately thick, hard-to-open husk. Inside, the flesh runs noticeably thick for a durian, roughly three-quarters of an inch or more, sweet and dense, with a pungent aroma typical of local Indonesian favorites. Grow grafted trees in rich, well-drained soil under consistent tropical warmth and humidity, since the species cannot tolerate any frost or prolonged cool spells. Let the spiny, oval, green-skinned fruit fall naturally rather than harvesting it early, and expect a tree to take several years of establishment before it fruits reliably.
sources: TFNet (International Tropical Fruits Network) -- Durian Varieties
Trubus Horticulture Magazine (Indonesia)
University of Hawaii CTAHR -- Durian for Hawaii

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in deep, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Si Mas comes from Rancamaya in Bogor, West Java, and is a national superior cultivar grown for its small, rounded, apple-like fruit.

directions: Si Mas is a Bogor-area national superior durian cultivar named for its glowing, bright-yellow flesh, which is thick, dry rather than wet, and finely fibered with a notably sweet taste and only moderately sharp aroma. The fruit itself is comparatively small and rounded, with a depressed base that gives it an apple-like outline, typically weighing a few pounds. Grow on deep, well-drained, humid tropical soil in full sun, since this cultivar, like all durian, needs sustained warmth without any winter chill to flower and fruit well. Because Si Mas is grown under several regional names across Java, confirm grafted stock traces to the original Rancamaya, Bogor selection before planting if cultivar purity matters.
sources: TFNet (International Tropical Fruits Network) -- Durian Varieties
Trubus Horticulture Magazine (Indonesia)
University of Hawaii CTAHR -- Durian for Hawaii

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in deep, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Matahari ('sun') hails from Cimanggu, Bogor, and is noted for strong resistance to the humid-climate pests and diseases common in its wet home region.

directions: Matahari takes its name, meaning 'sun,' from flesh of a bright golden-yellow that recalls sunlight, a trait that sets it apart among Bogor-area durian selections. Each roughly oval, greenish-brown, 4-to-8-pound fruit holds 10 to 20 flesh-filled lobes with comparatively sparse, pointed, slightly hooked spines, and the thick, smooth, dry-but-oily flesh carries a sweet flavor without an overpowering aroma. Because it developed in Bogor's famously wet, high-rainfall climate, Matahari shows above-average tolerance for the pests and fungal pressure that come with humid tropical growing conditions, though it still needs full sun and well-drained soil to perform. Grow grafted trees in deep, fertile ground and never let young plants experience chilling temperatures, as durian has no cold hardiness at any life stage.
sources: TFNet (International Tropical Fruits Network) -- Durian Varieties
Trubus Horticulture Magazine (Indonesia)
University of Hawaii CTAHR -- Durian for Hawaii

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in deep, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Sukun originated near Karanganyar, Central Java, and takes its name (Javanese for 'seedless') from its underdeveloped, shrunken seeds and extra-thick flesh.

directions: Sukun is an older Central Javanese durian selection whose Javanese name means 'seedless,' describing seeds that routinely fail to develop fully, leaving behind unusually thick, pale yellowish-white flesh in their place. The fruit runs long and rounded with a thin, easily opened yellowish husk bearing small, closely set spines, and the variety is historically significant as one of the parent lines behind the modern Monthong cultivar. Because true seeds are scarce or absent, propagate Sukun exclusively by grafting onto durian rootstock rather than attempting to grow it from seed. Give grafted trees deep, well-drained soil, full sun, and steady warmth and humidity year-round, as this cultivar has shown useful field tolerance to Phytophthora root rot but still has no cold tolerance whatsoever.
sources: Universitas Sebelas Maret (UNS) -- Sukun Durian Morphological Characterization
TFNet (International Tropical Fruits Network) -- Durian Varieties
University of Hawaii CTAHR -- Durian for Hawaii

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in deep, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Bawor was bred in Banyumas, Central Java, by grower Sarno Ahmad Darsono starting in 1996 and released around 2000 from crosses among roughly twenty local and foreign durian types.

directions: Bawor is a relatively young Banyumas-bred durian cultivar created by crossing roughly twenty local and imported durian lines, including Monthong, Petruk, and other named Javanese selections, to combine large fruit size with thick flesh and small seeds. Mature fruit commonly weighs 13 to 20 pounds and occasionally much more, with thin skin giving way to soft, creamy, yellow-to-orange flesh carrying a sweet flavor that can turn slightly bitter and alcohol-like as fruit over-ripens. Grow grafted trees in deep, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun with reliable warmth and humidity, since this is a true tropical durian with no frost tolerance at any stage. Growers report that flavor intensifies and sweetness increases during drier stretches of the growing season, so reducing irrigation slightly as fruit nears maturity can improve eating quality.
sources: Dinas Pariwisata Provinsi Jawa Tengah (Central Java Tourism Office)
Specialty Produce -- Bawor Durian Facts
Trubus Horticulture Magazine (Indonesia)

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery offshoots in spring in humus-rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial shade; Gula Pasir ('granulated sugar') is the smallest and sweetest of the many named Salak Bali strains from the Sibetan highlands of eastern Bali.

directions: Salak Gula Pasir, literally 'sand sugar' salak, is the most prized of the many named Salak Bali strains grown around the Sibetan highlands of eastern Bali, distinguished from ordinary salak by noticeably smaller fruit and an intensely sweet, almost sugary flavor with virtually no tartness. The round, blackish-brown-skinned fruit encloses white flesh divided into three lobes, usually around a single small seed or none at all, which is part of why this strain commands the island's highest salak prices. As with other salak, grow this clumping, spiny-stemmed palm as an understory plant in rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil beneath taller shade trees, and keep a male plant nearby or hand-pollinate female flowers to ensure fruit set. Thin crowded suckers and remove spent fronds regularly, and pick fruit clusters once the overlapping scales lift slightly and feel firm but not hard.
sources: Smithsonian Magazine -- Meet the Salak
PROSEA (Plant Resources of South-East Asia)
Bali tourism and agricultural extension sources on Salak Bali strains

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in rich, moist, well-drained soil in full sun sheltered from strong wind; Lebak Bulus takes its name from the Lebak Bulus area of South Jakarta and was officially released as a superior Indonesian cultivar by the Ministry of Agriculture in 1985.

directions: Lebak Bulus is one of Indonesia's longest-recognized rambutan cultivars, released as a superior variety by the Ministry of Agriculture in 1985 and named for the Lebak Bulus district of South Jakarta where it originated. Ripe fruit shows pinkish-red skin covered in relatively short, soft spines, and the sweet, juicy flesh is well known for separating cleanly from the seed, a trait Indonesian growers prize for easy fresh eating. Grow grafted trees in deep, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun with some shelter from strong wind, keeping moisture steady from flowering through fruit development. As with all rambutan, this cultivar has no frost tolerance and needs consistently warm, humid, essentially tropical conditions to fruit well.
sources: Indonesian Ministry of Agriculture cultivar release records
TFNet (International Tropical Fruits Network)
University of Hawaii CTAHR

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in rich, moist, well-drained soil in full sun sheltered from strong wind; Sinyonya is a West Javanese cultivar ranked among Indonesia's five leading commercial rambutan selections, prized for thick flesh and a seed that drops free cleanly.

directions: Sinyonya is a West Javanese rambutan cultivar counted among Indonesia's five leading commercial rambutan selections, recognized by dark red to wine-colored skin covered in fine, densely packed spines. The flesh runs thicker than many other rambutan cultivars and is sweet with a light tartness, and its small seed separates cleanly away from the flesh, making it popular for fresh markets. Grow grafted trees on deep, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun with wind protection, since Sinyonya's vigorous, sturdy growth habit also makes it a favored rootstock for grafting other rambutan selections. Provide steady moisture through flowering and fruit set, and protect trees from any cold exposure, as rambutan tolerates no frost at any stage of growth.
sources: Mistriyani et al., Morphological characterization of Indonesian rambutan cultivars (myfoodresearch.com)
TFNet (International Tropical Fruits Network)
University of Hawaii CTAHR

planting.note: Transplant seedlings or direct sow into warm, flooded paddy beds; Rojolele is an indigenous tropical-japonica lowland rice from Delanggu village, Klaten, Central Java, grown for its aromatic, soft-cooking premium grain.

directions: Rojolele is a traditional Indonesian lowland rice from Delanggu village in Klaten, Central Java, grown for generations for its fragrant, soft-textured cooked grain that commands premium prices in local markets. The plant grows notably tall, with sturdy stems, thick rough leaves, long panicles, and a deep root system, and typically needs around 150 days from sowing to grain maturity, considerably longer than modern short-duration rice. Grow it in well-flooded, fertile paddy fields with full sun, and stake or otherwise support stands in windy conditions, since the tall, heavy-headed plants are prone to lodging as the grain fills. Because it is a long-duration landrace, plan the growing calendar around a full warm season and expect lower yields and more drought sensitivity than high-yield modern rice varieties bred for the same region.
sources: Rojolele: A Premium Aromatic Rice Variety in Indonesia (ResearchGate/Preprints review)
Research on Rojolele Srinuk rice farming, Delanggu, Klaten (ResearchGate)
International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) genebank records

planting.note: Transplant seedlings or direct sow into warm, flooded paddy beds; Pandan Wangi is a javanica rice landrace with legally protected Geographical Indication status tied to the volcanic soils of Cianjur, West Java.

directions: Pandan Wangi is a javanica-type Indonesian rice landrace from Cianjur, West Java, named for cooked grain that carries a natural pandan-leaf fragrance from the same aromatic compound found in true pandan leaves, alongside a soft, slightly sticky texture. It is a late-maturing variety, typically needing roughly 150 to 160 days from sowing to harvest, longer than most modern rice. Grow it in well-flooded paddy fields in full sun on the mineral-rich volcanic soils it is traditionally associated with, since growers and buyers alike report that the variety partially loses its characteristic aroma when grown outside the Cianjur highlands. Cianjur-grown Pandan Wangi carries legal Geographical Indication protection in Indonesia, so seed and grain sold under the name elsewhere may not develop the same fragrance even under similar paddy management.
sources: Jurnal Pangan -- Penguatan Indikasi Geografis Beras Pandanwangi Cianjur
Design and Development of an Electronic Nose for Detecting Pandanwangi Rice Aroma Quality (research journal)
Indonesian Geographical Indication registry documentation

planting.note: Transplant seedlings or direct sow into warm, flooded paddy beds; Cempo Ireng is a traditional Javanese black rice landrace high in anthocyanin pigment, grown as a specialty health food rather than a daily staple.

directions: Cempo Ireng is a traditional Javanese black rice landrace, grown mainly in Yogyakarta and Central Java, whose deep purple-black bran layer comes from unusually high anthocyanin pigment levels that give the cooked grain its color and have made it popular as a specialty antioxidant-rich food rather than an everyday staple. Plants grow tall with a notably long vegetative phase, often taking around 150 days to mature, markedly longer than typical modern white-rice varieties grown in the same regions. Grow it in fertile, well-flooded paddy fields in full sun, and plan for extra vigilance against lodging and against birds and earhead bugs, both of which are drawn to the dark-hulled, late-ripening heads. Because yields tend to run lower and management more demanding than modern short-stature rice, most farmers grow Cempo Ireng as a premium side crop for the health-food market rather than a primary grain crop.
sources: Evaluation of Agronomy Character of Irradiated Black Rice Cempo Ireng Mutant Strains (ResearchGate)
Black Rice as a Functional Food in Indonesia (academic review)
Screening of Resistant Indonesian Black Rice Cultivars Against Bacterial Leaf Blight (Euphytica/Springer)
